fields.why: The note says R t was 'not estimated' if fewer than 10 ED visits were reported, and the Table shows such cells; the brief classes suppression of estimates as a transformation. B's test (probability that R t >1 judged against thresholds) is defensible, as decided under has_test.

Categories are set by the posterior probability that R t exceeds the fixed value 1 (e.g., growing if >90%), which works like a one-sided interval judged against 1 ('CI vs fixed value'). Reading the cutpoints as quantization of a probability measure (A) is also defensible.

The reported contrasts set the real-time categories against later ED data at four time points and across jurisdictions, which is group. B's fixed referent (R t = 1) is the threshold inside the category definition and is defensible only if the test reading is taken as the primary contrast.
This follows has_test. If the probability threshold against R t = 1 counts as 'CI vs fixed value', inference is tests; otherwise it is none, since no CIs are reported.

The report evaluates how a real-time surveillance indicator performs against later, complete data, and no design value names this (diagnostic accuracy needs computed accuracy measures). B's mixed/other fits better than trend; a rule such as 'surveillance-indicator or nowcast evaluation → mixed/other' would decide it.

The New Mexico counts are NSSP state-level ED data (note: 'count data are accessible to public health authorities in their respective jurisdiction'; the Table is sourced to NSSP). New Mexico granted publication permission, but no separate state system is analyzed.

brief_issues: The brief does not say whether a Bayesian posterior-probability threshold against a fixed value (P(R t >1) >90%) counts as 'CI vs fixed value' or as quantization. It also has no study_design value for evaluating a surveillance indicator or nowcast against later data.
